sources.citation: EG4 Electronics LLC — 'Modbus RTU Protocol' V58, 2023-10-28, 42 pp (vendor document; no model named inside). Committed at docs/eg4-modbus-rtu-protocol-v58.pdf

transport: RS-485 · Modbus RTU · 19200 8N1 · slave ID 1 · FC 0x03 (hold) / 0x04 (input) / 0x06 / 0x10 · min 1 s poll interval · max 40 registers per request (127 on newer firmware)
blocks: input 0–39 real-time · input 40–79 cumulative energy + fault/warning + temperatures · input 80–112 BMS/closed-loop battery block · input 113–174 parallel, serial number, generator, EPS L1N/L2N, AFCI, Pload · hold 0–199 settings (time, function-enable bitfields at 21 / 110 / 179, charge and discharge limits, AC-charge windows)
refutedOnReview: REFUTED as a six-model grouping, though the underlying map is real for two of the six.  WHAT CHECKS OUT: docs/eg4-modbus-rtu-protocol-v58.pdf exists locally at sha256 7dbea2032fc6314a193badecd2c75a06ab6f0eea0a6b5389ef7e54f57324a633, 42 pp, V58 2023-10-28, EG4electronics LLC. Section 2 states RS-485, 19200 bps, 8N1, min poll 1 s, max 40 registers per request grouped 0-39 / 40-79 / 80-119 — all as claimed. I downloaded
gotchas: Confidence split: the register map is vendor-doc, but membership in this dialect is only community-single for 12000XP, FlexBOSS18 and FlexBOSS21 (one author's stack). 6000XP and 18kPV-12LV are named on the vendor PDF's distribution filenames; 12kPV has an independent implementation.

FRAMING CONTRADICTION — do not build to the doc blindly. The doc's request/response tables (Tables 4/5/6) insert a 10-byte serial-number field SN[0]..SN[9] between the function code and the start address. Every working RS-485 implementation found (galets via libmodbus, poldim via pymodbus, HotNoob) uses PLAIN Modbus RT

BYTE-ORDER CONTRADICTION. Doc §2.7 says a 16-bit value 0x01 0x02 'should be parsed as 0x0201', and §2.8 says a 32-bit value 0x01 0x02 0x03 0x04 'should be parsed as 0x04030201'. Implementations do not do this: they read register values as ordinary big-endian Modbus registers and only swap the WORD order for 32-bit pair

Read grouping is enforced by firmware: a request may cover at most 40 registers AND must not straddle a 40-register group boundary (0–39, 40–79, 80–119, …). Reading 38–40 needs two requests. Newer firmware raises the cap to 127. A naive sequential reader gets exception 0x02/0x03.

Polling budget: the doc requires ≥1 s between queries, and ≥60 s if the WiFi dongle is left plugged in — the dongle shares the same RS-485 bus and the doc explicitly says to unplug it for frequent local polling.
